column2: When the gate shut behind you, a sentry poured a bowl of wine on the ground: for those on the road, he said. Which ones, you asked; he did not answer, only lifted his lantern higher. On its paper, in ink long faded: "The Thousand Li, out through the pass in the seventh month, three hundred camels." Not one of that caravan came back, ten years ago. Now the court opens the road again, and the first to go out are you.
column3: 关门在身后合上时，守卒往地上泼了一碗酒，说是敬路上的人。你问敬哪些人，他不答，只把灯笼挑高了些。灯笼纸上有一行褪了色的墨字：「千里号，丁未年七月出关，计驼三百」。十年前出关的那支商队，没有一个人回来。如今朝廷重开商路，第一支出关的，是你们。

column2: A broken banner stands on the beacon tower, its corners torn to threads by the wind. The bandits below are in no hurry; they seem to wait for someone to speak first. Their leader whistles, and every rider on the slope slaps his blade on his saddle at once, too evenly for men.
column3: 烽燧上插着一面断旗，旗角已经被风撕成了絮。墩下的马贼不着急动手，像是在等谁先开口。他们的首领打了个唿哨，满坡的人一齐把刀拍在马鞍上，声音整齐得不像人。

column2: Only an old postmaster lives at the post. He lights twelve lamps every night; every morning one is out, its oil untouched. "That one is for the guest," he says, writing your names into his book stroke by stroke. On the page before, the last name is still wet: Thousand Li, the bookkeeper.
column3: 驿站里只住着一个老驿丞。他每晚点十二盏灯，第二天清早，总有一盏是灭的，灯油一滴不少。「少的那盏，是给借宿的人留的。」他说着，把你们的名字一笔一划记进簿子里。你瞥见上一页最后一个名字，墨迹还是湿的：千里号·账房。

column2: The wind in the gorge learns to talk. Camel bells first, then someone calling, "Wait for us, wait." The sand robbers lie in the sound of it, and rush you the moment you turn your heads.
column3: 谷里的风会学人说话。先是驼铃，再是有人喊「停一停，等等我们」。沙匪就埋伏在风声里，等你们回头的那一瞬间扑上来。

column2: For a hundred li this is the only well, and a gang keeps it chained: a bucket of water for a bolt of silk. When the lid comes off, a film of fine gold dust floats on the water.
column3: 方圆百里只有这一口井，被一伙恶霸用铁链锁着，一桶水换一匹绢。打开井盖，水面上浮着一层细细的金粉。

column2: Price boards still hang on the ruined walls: "A cart of stone for a cart and a half of timber." You clear out a few mud rooms and raise the court's banner. Next morning foreign traders lead their camels up and knock, as if they had been waiting all along.
column3: 残墙上还钉着当年的价牌：「石一车，易木一车半」。你们清出几间土屋，挂起朝廷的旗。第二天清早，墙外就有胡商牵着骆驼来叩门，像是一直在等。

column2: Some nameless incense burns in the tent. The trader's eyes are grey; he says he has bought and sold in these sands for thirty years, anything at all, only never for copper.
column3: 帐里熏着说不出名字的香。胡商的眼睛是灰的，他说他在这片沙里做了三十年买卖，什么都卖，只是不收铜钱。

column2: The men on the ridge wear fox skins, and their eyes catch the light at night. They take no goods, only people. "Give us the ledger and you may pass," says their leader. But you carry no ledger.
column3: 岭上的人披着狐皮，夜里眼睛会反光。他们不劫货，只劫人。领头的说：「把账本交出来，就放你们过去。」可你们身上没有账本。

column2: A stele with no inscription stands by the road. In the torchlight, line after line of small characters rises on its face: names, each with goods. "So-and-so, silk twenty, tea forty." The last line is only now appearing. It is the name of one of your own men.
column3: 路边立着一块没有字的碑。拿火把一照，碑面上浮出一行一行的小字，全是人名，后面跟着货物：「某某，绢二十，茶四十」。最后一行刚刚浮出来，写的是开拓队里一个兵的名字。

column2: On the walls of the old fort stands a one-eyed bandit chief they call the Hawk. He will not stand aside, nor bargain. "Ten years ago I let a caravan through here," he says. "Since then, every night, camels come and kneel outside my tent." Behind him, horsemen spread out on both wings.
column3: 故垒的城头上站着一个独眼的马贼头子，人称「鹞子」。他不让路，也不谈价。「十年前我在这里放过一支商队，」他说，「后来每天夜里，都有骆驼来我帐外跪着。」他身后两翼的骑兵已经摆开了阵势。

column2: The quicksand swallows people, and spits them out again. Those it gives back wear the clothes of ten years ago; their eyes are empty, and they stand across the road and will not let you pass.
column3: 流沙会吞人，也会吐人。吐出来的人都穿着十年前的衣裳，眼神空空的，拦在路上不让你们走。

column2: All night camel bells ring outside the camp, circling and circling. At dawn the sand is full of hoofprints, three hundred rings around the camp, not one more, not one fewer.
column3: 整整一夜，营地外都有驼铃响，一圈一圈地绕。天亮时沙地上满是蹄印，围着营地踩了三百圈，一圈不多，一圈不少。

column2: The sky goes black all at once. Men with blades burst out of the storm, strike once and shrink back into the wind. When it dies down there is not one body on the ground.
column3: 天一下子黑了。沙暴里有人举着刀冲出来，砍完一刀又缩回风里。等风停了，地上一具尸体都没有。

column2: A crescent of water lies between the dunes, dry in no thousand years. The caravan boss who holds it says the spring is a mirror for the dead. You look down: the column in the water is dozens longer than the one on the bank.
column3: 一弯泉水卧在沙山之间，千年不涸。占泉的马帮头领说，泉水是给死人照镜子的。你们低头一看，水里映出的队伍比岸上多出好几十人。

column2: Only on nights of the full moon does a street light up deep in the sea of sand. The stall-keepers never look up, never speak, only hold out their hands to name a price. You trade timber for grain; the grain is new, but the sacks are stamped "Thousand Li." From then on, every night, the ghost market keeps a stall for you.
column3: 只有月圆的夜里，沙海深处才会亮起一条街。摊主们不抬头，不说话，只伸出手比价。你们拿木头换了粮，拿来的粮是新的，装粮的麻袋上却印着「千里号」。从此每晚，鬼市都给开拓队留一个摊位。

column2: A great caravan rests here, its tents a small town. Its leader is a woman with an eastern accent. Everything she sells is good, and she never lowers a price.
column3: 一支大驼队在这里歇脚，帐篷连成了一座小城。领队是个女人，说话带着东边的口音。她卖的东西都很好，就是价钱从来不肯少。

column2: Earthen mounds stand one after another like a sleeping white dragon. The bandits use them as a maze, shooting from behind them as you wind through.
column3: 土台一座连着一座，像一条睡着的白龙。马贼把这里当作迷宫，绕着土台放冷箭。

column2: The wind peels back a dune and half a city appears. The board over its gate reads "Thousand Li." Inside, the market stands in perfect order, sand thick on every shelf; on the counting desk, under a weight, an unsealed letter: "The goods arrived. The men did not."
column3: 风掀开沙丘，露出半座城。城门上的匾额写着「千里」二字。城里的市集摆得整整齐齐，货架上落满了沙，账台上压着一封没封口的信：「货已到，人未归」。

column2: Every bandit in the sea of sand pays tribute to this golden tent. The Bandit King sits on a throne of camel bone; three hundred names are carved on its back. "They owe me road money," he says, "and have not paid it yet. Have you come to pay for them?"
column3: 沙海里所有的马贼都向这顶金帐纳贡。马贼王坐在一张驼骨椅上，椅背上刻着三百个名字。「他们欠我的路钱，」他说，「到今天还没还清。你们来替他们还？」

column2: The cliff is honeycombed with niches, a Buddha seated in each. The ambush hides behind the statues; arrows fly from between the Buddhas' fingers.
column3: 崖壁上凿满了窟龛，每一龛里都坐着一尊佛。伏兵就藏在佛像后面，箭从佛的指缝里射出来。

column2: The mural in the hundred-and-twentieth cave shows a caravan. The old monk who keeps the caves says it is never the same two days running: yesterday the camels were still inside the pass, today they have crossed the sea of sand. Look closely: on the last camel sits someone exactly like you.
column3: 第一百二十窟的壁画上画着一支商队。守窟的老僧说，这画每天都不一样：昨天驼队还在关内，今天已经过了沙海。你们细看，画里最后一峰骆驼背上，坐着一个和你一模一样的人。

column2: Warrior monks with iron staves guard the caves; they say you carry "something unclean" and may not enter the mountain. Ask them what, and they chant a line of scripture as one and charge.
column3: 僧兵们拿着铁棍守在窟前，说开拓队身上带着「不干净的东西」，不许进山。问他们是什么东西，他们齐声念了一句经，就冲了上来。

column2: Before the temple gate stands a shed for giving out gruel, seized by false monks who charge a tael a bowl. When they are gone the real monks return; the shed, they say, was put up ten years ago for a caravan, and the gruel has been kept on the boil ever since. No one came to eat it.
column3: 寺门前搭着施粥的棚子，被一伙假和尚霸占，一碗粥要一两银子。赶走他们以后，真正的僧人回来了，说这棚子十年前就是为一支商队搭的，粥一直熬着，没人来喝。

column2: The cave is piled with sutras, and with ledger after ledger recording every trade along this road. You copy out the prices of a few old routes and send to ask: every one of them still holds.
column3: 洞里堆满了经卷，还有一摞一摞的账册，记着这一路上所有的买卖。你们从账册里抄出几条老商路的价钱，派人去问，竟都还作数。

column2: The painters gild and colour the caves, and paint portraits too: a good likeness, they say, adds ten years to a life. They sell other things besides, and never ask where they came from.
column3: 画匠们给石窟描金上彩，也替人画像。他们说，画得像的，人就能多活十年。他们也卖别的东西，从不问来路。

column2: A stretch of the gallery between the upper and lower caves has fallen away. Men stand at the far edge watching you, holding the Thousand Li's tallies of ten years ago.
column3: 连接上下窟的栈道断了一截。对面的人站在断口上看着你们，手里拿着当年千里号的令牌。

column2: In the deepest cave sits a great Buddha with no face. Before it burn three hundred lamps; more than half have gone out. Each lamp that goes out, the old monk says, is one of the Thousand Li who has "arrived." Arrived where, he does not know.
column3: 最深的一窟里坐着一尊没有脸的大佛。佛前供着三百盏灯，灭了一大半。老僧说：灯灭一盏，就有一个千里号的人「到了」。到了哪里，他也不知道。

column2: The Master wears a golden mask and says he has kept this mountain for ten years. "Those you seek," he says, "are all on this wall." Three hundred merchants are painted there, every face scraped away. He lifts a hand; the gold-masked guards behind him draw as one.
column3: 洞主戴着一张金色的面具，自称守着这座山已经十年。「你们要找的人，」他说，「都在这面墙上。」墙上画着三百个商人，每个人的脸都被刮掉了。他抬手，身后的金面卫一齐拔刀。

column2: A troop holds the fort outside the royal city, in armour of an old style from inside the pass. Their orders are to let no caravan in; for ten years they have kept them.
column3: 王城外的戍堡里驻着一队兵，穿的是关内的旧式甲胄。他们奉命不许任何商队进城，十年来一直如此。

column2: Everyone in the city knows of "the bookkeeper": his sums are never wrong; he came ten years ago and has kept the king's treasury ever since. At the inn a letter from him awaits you. It holds one line: "The lamp at White-Bone Post: I lit it."
column3: 城里人人都知道一个「账房先生」，说他算账从不出错，十年前来到这里，帮国王管了国库。你们在客栈收到他的一封信，信里只写了一句话：「白骨驿那盏灯，是我点的。」

column2: The vine trellises make a green sea, and the ambush hides beneath. Every blade bears the same mark: a camel carrying a lamp on its back.
column3: 葡萄架连成一片绿海，伏兵就藏在藤下。他们的刀上都刻着同一个记号：一峰骆驼，背上驮着一盏灯。

column2: The queen's brother's men hold the hostel, to squeeze foreign merchants. When they are thrown out, an old servant sets wine and food before you, and says it was all laid by ten years ago.
column3: 驿馆被国舅的家丁占着，专门敲诈外来的商人。把他们赶出去以后，馆里的老仆给你们备了酒饭，说这都是十年前就备下的。

column2: The hall hangs the banners of every nation but one. When you raise the court's banner in its place, every merchant in the hall rises to his feet. From this day the goods of the west can go straight back through the pass.
column3: 商馆里挂着各国的旗，独缺一面。你们把朝廷的旗挂上去的时候，满堂的商人都站了起来。从这天起，西域的货能直接运回关内了。

column2: The West Market has everything; someone even sells medicine for long life. An old man with a white beard keeps a small gourd: the pills in it, he says, let a man "begin again." He sells one a day.
column3: 西市里什么都有，连长生的药都有人卖。一个白胡子老人守着一只小葫芦，说这里面的丹药能让人「从头再来」，一天只卖一颗。

column2: The Golden Masks are the king's own guard, in the same masks as the Master of the Thousand Buddhas. They do not speak, nor eat, nor sleep at night; they only drill, over and over.
column3: 金面卫是国王的亲军，戴着和千佛洞主一样的面具。他们不说话，不吃饭，夜里也不睡觉，只是一遍一遍地操练。

column2: The king holds a banquet for you. The tables are full of guests, and not one of them touches his chopsticks. The king raises his cup: "To the Thousand Li." The hall raises its cups after him, and only then do you see: every guest has the same character sewn into his cuff. "Thousand."
column3: 国王设宴款待开拓队。宴席上坐满了宾客，一个个都不动筷子。国王举杯：「敬千里号。」满堂宾客跟着举杯，你这才看清，他们袖口上都缝着同一个字：「千」。

column2: The man on the throne lifts off his crown, and his face is an ordinary one. "I am the bookkeeper," he says. "Ten years ago I got one sum of the caravan's wrong, and from that day they have stood still on the road, unable to move a step." He rises; the Golden Masks form up on either side. "If you would pass, first settle that account."
column3: 王座上的人摘下了王冠，露出一张平凡的脸。「我就是那个账房，」他说，「十年前我把商队的账算错了一笔，从那天起，他们就停在了路上，一步也走不动。」他站起来，金面卫列阵护在两侧。「要过去，就先把这笔账算清。」

column2: The tax clerk checks your goods and stamps the back of your pass twice. Why twice, you ask. "One for you," he says, "and one for the mule train I never finished stamping, ten years ago." He presses a mouldy brick of tea into your hand, Thousand Li pressed into it. "They said they would be back when the tea ran out.
column3: 茶关的税吏验完货，在通关文书背面盖了两个印。你问为什么是两个，他说：「一个给你们，一个给十年前没盖完的那支马帮。」他把一块发霉的茶砖塞进你手里，砖上压着「千里号」三个字。「他们走的时候说，茶砖吃完就回来。」

column2: The brigands at the pass take no tea, only horses. The horses come back on their own the next day, a string of bells on each saddle, every clapper pulled out.
column3: 垭口上的山匪不劫茶，专劫马。被劫走的马第二天自己回来，鞍子上挂着一串铜铃，铃舌全被拔掉了。

column2: The fog is so thick you cannot see your own hands. Someone in the post is calling the roll, name by name, and each name answers "Here." None of you said a word, yet in the roll book every one of your names has been ticked.
column3: 雾浓得看不见自己的手。驿站里有人在点名，一个名字一个名字念过去，念到的人就应一声「到」。你们谁也没出声，可点名簿上，你们的名字后面都画了勾。

column2: The porters carry bales of tea taller than themselves, sixty li of mountain a day. Their chief says they owe the mule train a debt, and your lives will pay it. The porters set down their bales and draw knives out of them.
column3: 背夫们背着比人还高的茶包，一天走六十里山路。寨主说他们欠了马帮的债，要拿开拓队的命来还。背夫们放下茶包，从里面抽出了刀。

column2: The fire in the hearth house has not gone out in ten years. A gang of deserters holds it, and travellers pay a bale of tea to sit by it. When they are gone, the keeper rakes an iron box out of the ashes: an unfinished receipt. "Received of the Thousand Li, forty loads of tea. Owing—"
column3: 锅庄里的火塘十年没熄过，被一伙兵痞占着，过路人要烤火得交一包茶。赶走他们以后，掌柜的从火塘灰里扒出一只铁盒，里面是一张没写完的收据：「收千里号茶四十驮，欠——」。

column2: Highlanders lead their horses down to trade for tea, so many loads for a horse, the same price for centuries. You set the official scales up again. The headman runs a finger along the notches on the beam. "I know this scale," he says.
column3: 番人牵着马来换茶，一匹马换几驮茶，几百年都是一个价。你们重新立起了官秤，番人的头人摸了摸秤杆上的刻痕，说：「这杆秤，我认得。」

column2: The innkeeper is mute and bargains with an abacus. Among his goods is one odd thing: a string of bells without clappers, priced above everything else.
column3: 客栈老板是个哑巴，用算盘跟人讲价。他卖的东西里有一样很怪：一串没有铃舌的铜铃，标价比别的都高。

column2: The miasma in the woods is green; one breath and your head swims. Native troops with wet cloths over their faces charge out of it, and you cannot tell whether they are men or shadows the fog has thickened into.
column3: 林子里的瘴气是绿色的，吸一口就头昏眼花。土兵们戴着湿布从雾里冲出来，你分不清他们是人，还是瘴气凝成的影子。

column2: The cliff is covered in what travellers have cut into it, mostly "So-and-so was here." Highest of all, cut deep: "Lu Jiu guarded the box this far. While I live, so does the box." Beneath it someone has since added, the ink still wet: "He does not live."
column3: 崖壁上刻满了过路人留的字，大多是「某某到此」。最高处有一行字，刻得很深：「陆九护匣至此，匣在人在」。字的下面，有人后来补了一句，墨还没干：「人不在了。」

column2: The Master of the Fog Posts lives in the last post and never shows himself. His voice comes from every side. "Ten years ago I called their roll: three hundred, not one missing. When they came out of the fog there were two hundred and ninety-nine." A ring of torches flares up in the fog; native troops close in from three sides. "Was the missing one you?"
column3: 雾驿主住在最后一座驿站里，从不露面。他的声音从四面八方传来：「十年前我替他们点过名，三百人，一个不少。可走出雾的时候，只剩下二百九十九。」雾里亮起一圈火把，土兵从三面围了上来。「少的那一个，是不是你？」

column2: The bamboo bridge takes one man at a time. On the far side the village guards play reed pipes; when the piping stops, a line of bamboo rafts rises from the river below, crowded with men.
column3: 竹桥只容一人通过，桥那头的寨兵吹着芦笙。笙声一停，桥下的河里就浮起一排竹筏，筏上站满了人。

column2: The gu woman pours each of you a bowl of wine: drink, she says, and you will not lose your way in the village. You do not drink. In the night someone hears his bowl turning on the table, round and round all night. Cut into its foot: the character for thousand.
column3: 蛊婆给每个人倒了一碗酒，说喝了就不会在寨子里迷路。你们没喝。夜里，有人听见自己的碗在桌上转圈，转了一整夜，碗底刻着一个「千」字。

column2: Stilt house rises over stilt house, and crossbowmen lie under the floorboards. Their bolts have no heads, only a thin thread, its other end tied who knows where.
column3: 吊脚楼一层叠一层，弩手就藏在楼板下面。他们射的箭不带箭头，只带一根细线，线的另一头不知道拴在哪里。

column2: The terraces grow nothing but antidotes, and a band of village men has fenced them off: a person for a basket. Once you scatter them, the growers bring herbs and dry rations. A man from the lowlands taught them to grow these ten years ago, they say. "More are coming after me," he told them.
column3: 药田里种的都是解毒的草，被一伙寨丁圈了起来，要拿人来换。你们打散了寨丁，药农们送来了草药和干粮，说这些草是十年前一个汉人教他们种的，他说「后面还有人要来」。

column2: The elders sit round the hearth and hear you out. The oldest takes half a brick of tea from his coat; set against the one you were given at Yazhou, the two halves make one whole. "The tea has come," he says. "The road may open."
column3: 寨老们围着火塘坐成一圈，听你们讲来意。最老的那个从怀里掏出半块茶砖，和你在雅州收到的那块一对，正好是一整块。「茶来了，」他说，「这条路就可以通了。」

column2: The silversmith's ornaments ward off gu: wear one and the worms keep away. He sells other things too, from the plains, from the snow mountains, from over the sea. All left by the mule train, he says.
column3: 银匠打的银饰能防蛊，戴上以后，蛊虫就不敢近身。他也卖别的东西，从中原来的、从雪山来的、从海那边来的，他说都是马帮当年留下的。

column2: A clay jar hangs from every tree in the forest, its mouth sealed with red cloth. The forest keeper opens one. What crawls out is no worm but threads of fog, and where the fog spreads, there are men.
column3: 林子里每一棵树上都挂着陶罐，罐口封着红布。守林人揭开一只罐子，里面爬出来的不是虫，是一缕一缕的雾。雾散开，就成了人。

column2: Ten years ago, the gu woman tells you, three hundred men of the mule train drank the bound-heart gu together. It harms no one. Only, from then on, the three hundred live and die together, and none may go on ahead. "So they wait," she says. "For the last of them to arrive."
column3: 蛊婆告诉你们，十年前马帮里有三百人，一起喝了同心蛊。同心蛊不害人，只是从此三百人同生同死，谁也不能先走一步。「所以他们一直在等，」她说，「等最后一个人走到。」

column2: The Gu King sits beside a great vat. In it lives a golden silkworm three inches long. "Three hundred hearts are tied to it," he says. "It has gone hungry ten years." He taps the rim of the vat; the reed pipes of the whole village sound at once, and warriors pour from every stilt house.
column3: 蛊王坐在一口大缸边，缸里养着一只三寸长的金蚕。「三百个人的心都拴在它身上，」他说，「它饿了十年了。」他敲了敲缸沿，寨子里的芦笙一齐响了起来，寨兵从四面的吊脚楼里涌了出来。

column2: A single rope slide crosses the river. The men on the far bank wait until you are halfway over before they start hacking at the rope.
column3: 江面上只有一根溜索。对岸的人等你们滑到一半，才开始砍绳子。

column2: Mule bells sound in the gorge, bells without clappers. The sound bounces from wall to wall, climbing, until it is lost in the clouds. You count: two hundred and ninety-nine.
column3: 峡谷里传来马铃声，可那些铃是没有铃舌的。声音从崖壁这头弹到那头，一路往上走，走到云里就没了。你们数了，一共二百九十九声。

column2: The gallery hangs on a sheer wall, half its beams rotten. The guards at the gate wear the mule train's livery of ten years ago, its lettering faded past reading.
column3: 栈道修在绝壁上，木桩一半已经朽了。关卡上的守兵穿着十年前马帮的号衣，号衣上的字已经褪得看不清了。

column2: The cave is stacked with hay and sacks of highland barley, and a band of stragglers holds it. Once they flee, you find a mark drawn in charcoal on the wall: a box, a lock on the box, an eye on the lock.
column3: 岩洞里堆着成捆的干草和成袋的青稞，被一伙流兵占了。打跑流兵以后，你们发现洞壁上用炭画着一个记号：一个箱子，箱子上画着一把锁，锁上画着一只眼睛。

column2: The post at the snow line was the mule train's last halt. The postmaster digs out a bill of goods from ten years ago. The last page reads: "Tea gone, horses gone, the box not yet." You open the post for business again; next day herders come down from the snows with their yaks.
column3: 雪线上的驿站是马帮最后一个歇脚的地方。驿丞翻出一本十年前的货单，最后一页写着：「茶尽，马尽，匣未尽。」你们把驿站重新开了张，雪山那边的人第二天就赶着牦牛来了。

column2: A line of lamas drives yaks down the mountain, laden with butter, wool cloth and things of no clear origin. The temple on the snow mountain, says the lama at their head, has not opened its doors in ten years.
column3: 一队喇嘛赶着牦牛往山下走，驮着酥油、氆氇和一些说不出来历的东西。领头的喇嘛说，雪山上的神庙已经十年没开过门了。

column2: The guards on Eagle-Beak Rock roll boulders down; after each volley someone shouts from the top, "Captain Lu says no one goes up the mountain."
column3: 鹰嘴岩上的守兵往下推石头，推完一轮，就有人在岩顶上喊：「陆镖头说了，谁也不许上山。」

column2: A letter is wedged in a crack in the rock, wrapped in oilcloth many times. The writer is Lu Jiu, captain of the Thousand Li's guard. "What is in the box must be shown to whoever comes. If they come from the court, open it; if not, send them home." On the cover, the addressee: Whoever Comes After.
column3: 岩缝里塞着一封信，油布包了好几层。写信的人叫陆九，是千里号马帮的镖头：「匣中之物，须面呈来人。来人若是朝廷的，就开匣；若不是，就让他回去。」信封上写着收信人：后来者。

column2: Lu Jiu, Captain of the Guard

At the end of the gallery a man stands deep in snow, as if he has stood there for years. The iron box on his back is fastened with three locks. "I gave my word," says Lu Jiu. "While I live, so does the box. To take it, first show me you can guard it better than I." The guards behind him draw together, their blades crusted with ice.
column3: 栈道的尽头站着一个人，身上落满了雪，像是站了很多年。他背上的铁匣上了三道锁。「我答应过的，」陆九说，「匣在人在。你们要拿走它，得先让我知道，你们比我更护得住它。」他身后的镖师们一齐拔刀，刀上都结着冰。

column2: The Temple on the Snow Mountain
Pilgrims circle the snow mountain, prostrating at every step. Warrior monks bar the road: no one goes up who has not gone round three times. You do not have time for three times.
column3: 转山的人一步一叩首，绕着雪山走。守山的武僧拦在路上，说没有转满三圈的人不能上山。你们没有时间转三圈。

column2: Every stone in the roadside cairn is carved with scripture, all but one. That one is carved with an account: "Thousand Li: tea, forty loads; horses, sixty; men, three hundred. Box, one." Beneath it someone has scratched with a fingernail, stroke after stroke, as if counting days.
column3: 路边的玛尼堆上，每块石头都刻着经文。有一块刻的不是经文，是一本账：「千里号，茶四十驮，马六十匹，人三百。匣一。」账的最后，有人用指甲划了一道，像是一笔一笔地在数日子。

column2: Men lie in wait on the snow slopes either side of the valley. They loose no arrows; they shout, all together. At the shout the snow comes down, and there are blades in it.
column3: 谷两边的雪坡上埋伏着人。他们不放箭，只是一齐大喊。喊声一起，雪就塌了下来，雪里裹着刀。

column2: Horse thieves hold the little monastery by the hot springs. When they are gone, the old lama brews you butter tea. It is the Thousand Li's tea, he says; he has rationed it ten years, and now he need not.
column3: 温泉边的小寺被一伙盗马贼占着。赶走他们以后，寺里的老喇嘛给你们煮了酥油茶。茶是千里号的茶，他说十年来一直省着喝，现在可以不用省了。

column2: Once a year the temple holds its fair, and everyone from above and below the snows comes. You lay out the court's goods; they are gone the first day. The temple steward hands you a bronze seal. "From now on, all trade up and down the mountain goes by this seal."
column3: 一年一度的庙会，雪山上下的人都来了。你们在集上摆开朝廷的货，头一天就卖空了。神庙的执事把一枚铜印交给你们：「从此以后，山上山下的买卖，都认这枚印。」

column2: A merchant lives below the sky burial ground and sells what others no longer need. Those who die on the mountain take nothing with them, he says. One thing he sells only one a day: a pill, for "someone who must begin again."
column3: 天葬台下住着一个商人，卖的都是别人用不着了的东西。他说，雪山上的人走的时候，什么都不带。他这里有一样东西一天只卖一颗，是一种丹药，说是留给「要从头再来的人」的。

column2: The guardians at the temple doors wear yak-headed masks and carry vajra clubs. Beneath the masks there are no faces, only fog, the very fog of Tea Pass.
column3: 神庙门前的护法戴着牛头面具，手持金刚杵。他们的面具下面没有脸，只有一团雾，和茶垭口的雾一模一样。

column2: The iron box opens. There is no gold or silver in it, only half a sea chart, and along its edge in small characters: "The land roads end here. The rest goes by sea." On the back of the chart is the court's seal, the very seal stamped twice at the Tea Gate of Yazhou.
column3: 铁匣打开了。里面没有金银，只有半张海图，海图的边上写着一行小字：「陆路已尽，余下的，走海路。」海图背面盖着朝廷的印，和雅州茶关那两个印，一模一样。

column2: In the great hall of the temple sits the mountain god, and the mountain god has Lu Jiu's face. "I promised them," it says, "to keep this road and wait for whoever came after." Outside a blizzard rises; the god's guardians close in from three sides. "Now you have come. Let me see whether you are fit to go on."
column3: 神庙的大殿里供着山神，山神的脸是陆九的脸。「我答应过他们，」山神说，「护住这条路，等后来的人。」殿外风雪大作，山神的护法从三面围了上来。「现在你们来了。让我看看，你们配不配接着走下去。」

column2: The harbour official takes the half chart you brought, draws the other half from a cabinet, and lays them together: they fit to a hair. "Ten years ago the Thousand Li's ship sailed from here," he says. "Its captain left half the chart behind and said that when the other half came back, someone would be able to find them." Out in the harbour an old ship is raising sail; the lantern at its stern bears the character for thousand.
column3: 市舶司的官员接过你们带来的半张海图，从柜子里取出另外半张，两张一拼，严丝合缝。「十年前千里号的船从这里出海，」他说，「船主把半张图留在这里，说等另一半回来，就有人能找到他们。」窗外的港口里，一条旧船正在升帆，船尾的灯笼上写着一个「千」字。

column2: The porters on the docks answer to a gang: pay, or your goods never reach a ship. The gang boss rolls two iron balls in his palm and says the Thousand Li never paid its berth, ten years ago.
column3: 码头上的苦力归一个帮会管，不交钱，货就上不了船。帮主手里盘着两颗铁胆，说千里号的船钱十年前就没付清。

column2: The temple's fortune cup holds a single slip, and whoever draws, it is this one: "The ship is here, the people are here, the lamp is here." A woman captain drew it ten years ago, says the keeper; since she sailed, it is the only slip left in the cup.
column3: 庙里的签筒里只有一支签，谁去抽都是这一支：「船在，人在，灯在。」庙祝说，这支签是十年前一个女船主求的，她走以后，签筒里的签就只剩下这一支了。

column2: The alleys of the foreign quarter are too narrow to pass but sideways. Sailors of every nation fight over the place and set on any stranger. Every blade is bound with the same red cord, tied in three hundred knots.
column3: 番坊的巷子窄得只容一人侧身。各国的水手在这里争地盘，见了生人就动手。他们的刀上都缠着一样的红绳，绳上打着三百个结。

column2: Pirates hold the shipyard and are tearing the keel out of an old hull. Once they are gone, the old shipwright says this ship was built to the Thousand Li's plans. Ten years he has worked on it, waiting for someone to sail her.
column3: 船坞被一伙海贼占了，正在拆一条旧船的龙骨。赶跑他们以后，老船匠说这条船就是照着千里号的图纸造的，他造了十年，就等有人来开。

column2: You spread the ledgers of the silk road and the tea road on the trade office's great desk, and the official checks them page by page. When he is done he adds a line to the customs book: "The Thousand Li may continue its voyage." From that day the goods of over the sea can come back along all three roads.
column3: 你们把丝路和茶路的账册摊在市舶司的大案上，官员一页一页地对。对完了，他在海关的簿子上添了一行：「准千里号续航」。从这天起，海那边的货，能顺着三条路一起回来了。

column2: The master of the shipping house is a one-armed old man with a lightning abacus. Among his goods are spices of the sand sea, butter of the snow mountains, and a golden mask from the silk road. The Thousand Li left them in his keeping, he says, and paid the fee ten years ago.
column3: 船行的掌柜是个独臂老人，账算得飞快。他卖的东西里有沙海的香料、雪山的酥油，还有一枚丝路上的金面具。他说，这些都是千里号寄存在这里的，寄存费十年前就付过了。

column2: The battery's orders are to let no ship with a thousand lantern out of the harbour. The order was given ten years ago, and no one has ever rescinded it.
column3: 炮台上的守兵接到的命令是：任何挂「千」字灯笼的船都不许出港。命令是十年前下的，没有人撤销过。

column2: The night before you sail every light in the harbour goes out but one, on your ship. At midnight someone knocks on the hull, once, twice, two hundred and ninety-nine times. At dawn two hundred and ninety-nine pairs of straw sandals stand neatly on the deck, their soles all wet.
column3: 出海前一夜，港口里所有的灯都灭了，只有你们的船上还亮着一盏。半夜里，有人敲船舷，一下，两下，一共二百九十九下。天亮时，甲板上整整齐齐地放着二百九十九双草鞋，鞋底都是湿的。

column2: The Dragon King of the Harbour

The Dragon King is the greatest merchant of Quanzhou. Ten years ago he bought every berth in the harbour, and left one empty. "That one is the Thousand Li's," he says. "Ten years I have waited for them to come back and pay for it. Will you pay for them?" At a wave of his hand, the war junks either side of the quay drop their gangways together.
column3: 「海龙王」是泉州最大的海商，十年前买下了港口所有的泊位，唯独留着一个空着。「那是千里号的，」他说，「我等了十年，等他们回来交泊位钱。你们替他们交？」他一挥手，码头两侧的楼船一齐落下了跳板。

column2: In the fog the reefs stand like rows of teeth. Pirate cutters slip between them under black sails, invisible in the fog. Only their oars can be heard.
column3: 雾里的礁石像一排排牙齿。海贼的快船在礁石间穿行，他们的船帆是黑的，在雾里根本看不见，只听得见桨声。

column2: A bottle drifts on the water with a note inside, in the hand of the bookkeeper of the silk road: "The sand sea is passed, the caves are passed, the oasis city is passed; what remains of the account is at sea." On the back, in Lu Jiu's hand from the tea road: "The box is handed over."
column3: 海面上漂着一只瓶子，瓶里塞着一张纸条，字迹是丝路上那个账房的：「沙海已过，佛窟已过，王城已过，余下的账在海上。」纸条背面，是茶路上陆九的字：「匣已交人。」

column2: A fleet appears all at once in the fog, ship lashed to ship in battle order. They fly the colours of a pirate band the court wiped out ten years ago, yet every man aboard is alive and breathing.
column3: 雾里突然出现了一支船队，船连着船，排成了阵。他们打的旗号是十年前就被朝廷剿灭的一伙海寇，可船上的人，一个个都活生生的。

column2: Water is life at sea, and the spring on this islet is guarded by pirates. When they are driven off you find a wooden board by the spring: "The Thousand Li drew water here. The rest is left for those who come after."
column3: 海上缺水，这座小岛上的泉眼就是命。一伙海盗把泉眼围了起来。赶走他们以后，你们在泉边发现了一块木牌：「千里号取水于此，余水留后来者。」

column2: Dozens of ships lashed together on the open sea make a market, and traders of every nation leap from deck to deck, haggling. When your ship comes alongside, every one of them stops and asks: "Has the Thousand Li come back?"
column3: 几十条船在海上并成一片，就是一个集市。各国的商人在船与船之间跳来跳去，讨价还价。你们的船一靠上来，所有的商人都停了手，问：「是千里号回来了吗？」

column2: A trader from the southern seas is laden with ivory, rhinoceros horn and pepper. Its captain, a smiling fat man, saw the Thousand Li at sea ten years ago, he says, sailing on east with its lamp always lit.
column3: 南洋来的商船装满了象牙、犀角和胡椒。船主是个笑眯眯的胖子，他说他十年前在海上见过千里号，那条船一直往东开，船上的灯一直亮着。

column2: Singers sit on the reef, and their song is so sweet that those who hear it steer for the rocks without knowing. Behind the singing waits a band of pirates who live off wrecks.
column3: 礁石上坐着唱歌的人，歌声很好听，听的人会不知不觉把船往礁石上开。歌声背后，是一伙专捞沉船的海贼。

column2: In the wreck of a sunken ship you haul up a logbook: the Thousand Li's. The last page reads: "The fog is too thick to see the stars. The captain says, follow the lamp. Three hundred, not one missing." The date is left blank.
column3: 你们在一条沉船的残骸里捞到了一本航海日志，是千里号的。最后一页写着：「雾太大，看不见星。船主说，跟着灯走。三百人，一个不少。」日期一栏是空的。

column2: The Admiral of the Fog's flagship stands three decks high, and on its bow is a man in court robes. "My orders are to stop the Thousand Li here," he says. "Ten years on, they have not been withdrawn." His warships fan out into a half moon behind him, every gun trained on you. "Are you the Thousand Li?"
column3: 雾海提督的旗舰有三层楼高，船头站着一个穿朝廷官服的人。「我奉命在这里截住千里号，」他说，「十年了，命令还没撤。」他身后的战船排成一个半圆，炮口齐齐对准了你们。「你们是千里号吗？」

column2: An upside-down city floats on the sea, its gates open. Its soldiers march out of it upside down, feet on the sky, blades pointing at the water.
column3: 海面上浮着一座倒过来的城，城门大开，守兵从城里倒着走出来，脚踩着天，刀尖朝下。

column2: Three roads appear in the mirage: one of yellow sand, one of snow mountains, one of sea. On each a caravan is travelling, and the leaders of all three turn round. All three faces are yours.
column3: 蜃楼里出现了三条路：一条是黄沙，一条是雪山，一条是海。三条路上都走着一支商队，商队最前面的人回过头来，三张脸，都是你的脸。

column2: The soldiers who charge out of the mirage wear the sheepskins of the silk road's bandits, the rattan armour of the tea road's highlanders, the short coats of the sea's pirates. Everyone you have fought along the way is here.
column3: 蜃楼里冲出来的兵，有的穿着丝路马贼的皮袍，有的穿着茶路土兵的藤甲，有的穿着海贼的短褂。你们一路上打过的人，都在这里。

column2: In the mirage stands a sea market whose goods are real and whose stallkeepers are not. Mirage soldiers hold it; once they are gone, the stallkeepers melt into smoke, but their goods stay behind.
column3: 蜃楼里有一座海市，摊子上的东西都是真的，就是摊主是假的。一伙蜃兵霸着集市，赶走以后，摊主们化成一缕烟，货却留了下来。

column2: There is a trade office in the mirage too, and its official is the very image of the one in Quanzhou. He opens his book: every deal of your whole journey is in it, to the last coin. "The accounts of the three roads," he says, "come together here."
column3: 蜃楼里也有一座市舶司，官员和泉州的那个长得一模一样。他翻开簿子，簿子上写着你们这一路的每一笔买卖，一笔不差。「三条路的账，」他说，「到这里就能对上了。」

column2: A merchant stands where the mirage meets the sea, half his body solid and half not. His goods are the same: some you can take hold of, some you cannot. The ones you can are very good.
column3: 一个商人站在蜃楼和大海的交界处，一半身子是实的，一半是虚的。他卖的东西也是这样，有的拿得到，有的拿不到。拿得到的那些，都很好。

column2: The sea is as flat as a mirror, and the ships in it are the ships above it. When the enemy in the mirror strikes, men above it bleed.
column3: 海面平得像镜子，镜子里的船和镜子外的船一模一样。镜子里的敌人砍一刀，镜子外的人就流一道血。

column2: As the mirage fades you see a woman: the leader of the caravan in the sand sea, the one with the eastern accent. "My name is Shen Du," she says. "The Thousand Li is my ship. The bookkeeper, Lu Jiu and I took three roads, to meet again at the Return Ruins. They have both arrived. Only the last one is missing."
column3: 蜃楼散去的时候，你们看见了一个女人，正是沙海驼队营地里那个说话带东边口音的女领队。「我叫沈渡，」她说，「千里号是我的船。账房、陆九和我，三个人分三路走，约好在归墟碰头。他们都到了，就差最后一个人。」

column2: The Mirage King is a clam too vast to see the edges of, and its breath is the mirage. Its voice rises as if from the seabed: "All that you have seen, I have kept in memory for them. Ten years I have remembered their roads, and I can hold them no longer." It opens its shell, and the armies of the mirage pour out together.
column3: 蜃王是一只大得看不见边的蛤，它吐出的气就是蜃楼。它的声音像是从水底传上来的：「你们看见的东西，都是我替他们记着的。我把他们的路记了十年，就快记不住了。」它张开壳，蜃楼里的兵马一齐冲了出来。

column2: Here the sea spins down into itself. A band of divers guards the maelstrom's edge: no ship that went down ever came up, they say, so they let no ship go down.
column3: 海水在这里打着旋往下沉。漩涡边上守着一队水鬼，他们说，下去的船从来没有上来过，所以他们不让船下去。

column2: Lights shine at the bottom of the maelstrom. One, two, three... you count to two hundred and ninety-nine. They are the same lamps as at White-Bone Post, the same as before the Faceless Buddha.
column3: 漩涡底下亮着灯，一盏，两盏，三盏……你数到二百九十九。这些灯和白骨驿的灯、无面佛前的灯，是同一种灯。

column2: The keels of sunken ships stand in a wall on the seabed. The men behind it bear weapons of every nation and age: all the sailors of ten years who never came home.
column3: 沉船的龙骨在海底排成了一道墙，墙后面的人用的是各国各代的兵器。他们是十年来所有没能回家的水手。

column2: In the heart of the Return Ruins lies an islet with a well whose water is fresh and smells of tea. Castaway pirates hold it. When they are gone you find three hundred bowls beside the well, the character for thousand cut into the foot of each.
column3: 归墟中央有一座小岛，岛上有一口井，打上来的是淡水，还带着茶香。占井的是一伙落难的海盗，打跑他们以后，你们在井边看见了三百只碗，碗底都刻着一个「千」字。

column2: The Thousand Li lies at anchor off the island, its hold untouched in ten years: silk, bricks of tea, porcelain, and a stack of ledgers. You put the accounts of the three roads together; they balance to the last coin. From this day the goods of all the world can travel the three roads.
column3: 千里号就停在岛边，货舱里的货十年没动过：丝绸、茶砖、瓷器，还有一摞账本。你们把三条路的账合在一起，整整齐齐，一笔不差。从这一天起，天下的货都能顺着三条路往来了。

column2: A market is laid out on the Thousand Li's deck, and the sellers are the ship's own people. They take no money; they only ask you to sign the ledger. An old man guards a little gourd whose pill, he says, lets a person "begin again."
column3: 千里号的甲板上摆开了一个集市，卖货的都是船上的人。他们不收钱，只要你在账本上签个名。有一个老人守着一只小葫芦，说里面的丹药能让人「从头再来」。

column2: The keepers of the ruins say nothing; they only guard the Thousand Li. Their faces are blank, like the Faceless Buddha, like the bells without clappers, like the empty berth.
column3: 守墟人不说话，只守着千里号。他们的脸上什么都没有，就像无面佛，像没有铃舌的铃，像空着的那个泊位。

column2: In the captain's cabin a sealed edict lies under lock. Shen Du hands it to you. "Ten years ago the court ordered that the three caravans should not open it until a second expedition had travelled the whole way." The edict holds only a roll: three hundred of the Thousand Li, two hundred and ninety-nine names, and the last line empty. Beside it, three words: Whoever Comes After.
column3: 船主舱里锁着一道圣旨。沈渡把它交给你：「十年前朝廷交代，三路商队要等到第二支开拓队走通全程，才能打开它。」圣旨上只有一张名单：千里号三百人，二百九十九个名字，最后一行空着，旁边写着三个字：后来者。

column2: In the deepest part of the Return Ruins the water is still. A man whose face cannot be made out sits there, two hundred and ninety-nine lamps behind him. "The road has reached its end," he says. "Someone must fill in the last line of the roll." He rises, and the lamps behind him light one by one, soldiers standing beneath every one. "Before you write, get past me. Then the Thousand Li will have arrived."
column3: 归墟的最深处，海水是静的。一个看不清面目的人坐在那里，身后是二百九十九盏灯。「路走到头了，」他说，「名单上最后一行，要有人填。」他站起来，身后的灯一盏一盏地亮了起来，灯下站满了兵。「填之前，先过我这一关。过了，千里号就到了。」
